author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner record
summary: The owner detail page offers a cancel action beside each upcoming visit (dated later than today). Cancelling removes that visit from the pet's record. Past visits show no cancel action and stay immutable.
acceptance_criteria: Given an owner's record with a pet that has an upcoming visit, when the record is shown, then a cancel action is offered beside that visit.
Given a pet's upcoming visit, when it is cancelled from the owner's record, then the visit no longer appears on that pet's record and the owner's record is shown again.
Given a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is shown, then no cancel action is offered beside that visit.
Given a cancel request naming a visit that does not belong to the named owner's pet, when it is submitted, then it is refused and nothing is removed.
Given a pet with several visits, when one is cancelled, then the pet's other visits remain listed.
non_goals: Amending a booked visit (date or description) — remains NG-5
Removing or deleting a past visit — remains NG-4
notes: Scope decision flagged for human confirmation: cancel applies ONLY to upcoming visits (visit date later than today), matching the 'upcoming visit' wording and the wrong-pet/wrong-day motivation, and reusing the same date boundary booking enforces (REQ-VIS-001). This reverses two standing non-goals — NG-4 (deleting a visit) and NG-5 (cancelling a visit once booked) — both now narrowed in the PRD. Whether cancellation is a hard delete or a retained-but-hidden state is a HOW decision left to system-design; the PRD states only that the visit no longer appears on the record.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Cancellation reuses the established owner-feature mutation pattern (system-design.md#contracts, #persistence): a POST handler in VisitController mutates the owner–pet–visit graph through the Owner aggregate and persists via owners.save(owner) — there is no VisitRepository. Three small pieces are genuinely new and recorded in durable memory: (1) a shared 'upcoming' predicate reifying the ubiquitous-language 'Upcoming Visit' term as Visit.isUpcoming() (date != null && date.isAfter(LocalDate.now())), the same boundary booking enforces in VisitController.processNewVisitForm, so the view (th:if) and the server-side guard agree on one source of truth; (2) an aggregate removal method on Owner mirroring the existing Owner.addVisit(petId, visit), delegating to Pet; (3) hard-delete semantics via orphan removal on Pet.visits (ADR 2026-08-05). Verified by reading VisitController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java and the three schema.sql files directly (IntelliJ oracle not connected in this dispatch).
integration_points: HTTP verb/route: use POST at /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel — every mutation in this app is a POST (no DELETE/PUT anywhere; server-rendered HTML forms only support GET/POST), mirroring booking's nested route. The template action must be a POST form, NOT an anchor, since it mutates; on success redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a flash 'message', matching processNewVisitForm.

Ownership guard: walk owner.getPet(petId) (already throws IllegalArgumentException when the pet is not the owner's — the existing wrong-pet booking guard) then locate the visit by id within pet.getVisits(); a visit not on that pet is refused and nothing is removed. Symmetric with edge-case-1 of Visits (wrong-pet booking).

Upcoming guard is defense-in-depth: hiding the cancel button in the view (th:if=${visit.upcoming}) is UX only; the POST handler must independently reject a non-upcoming (past/today) visit, exactly as processNewVisitForm re-checks the date server-side even though the form defaults it forward. Both use Visit.isUpcoming().

i18n (REQ-LANG-002): the cancel action label must be a new message key added to EVERY locale bundle under src/main/resources/messages/, not hard-coded in the template. Follow the existing #{addVisit}/#{editPet} pattern.

patterns.description: Owner.addVisit(petId, visit) — the aggregate write path to mirror for removal; resolves the pet via getPet(petId) and Asserts it, then delegates to the Pet
processNewVisitForm — the POST-mutate-save-redirect shape and the server-side date-boundary check to reuse for the upcoming guard
the per-visit row (th:each visit : pet.visits) where the cancel form is placed beside each upcoming visit

risks.risk: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit is an @ModelAttribute("visit") method that runs before EVERY handler in the controller and grafts a fresh blank Visit onto the pet (pet.addVisit(new Visit())). Added to the cancel POST, this blank Visit rides along on the loaded pet; with cascade=ALL it is a transient new entity that owners.save(owner) will cascade-INSERT, and Spring Boot's default pre-persist bean validation would reject its null @NotBlank description — breaking cancel. In @WebMvcTest the mocked repository returns the SAME Owner instance on every findById, so the polluted graph is the one saved; in production each findById returns a fresh instance, so the bug's visibility differs between test and prod.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the blank Visit injected by loadPetWithVisit is never persisted on the cancel path. Cleanest: narrow loadPetWithVisit so the new-Visit creation happens only on the booking handlers (initNewVisitForm/processNewVisitForm) rather than in the shared @ModelAttribute, leaving the shared method to load owner+pet only — booking behaviour is pinned by the existing processNewVisitForm* tests. If the implementer finds this entanglement forces an awkward extension, raise a consultation-request rather than persisting a filtered graph.

risks.risk: Naive collection remove would orphan, not delete: Pet.visits is a unidirectional @OneToMany(@JoinColumn pet_id) without orphanRemoval, and pet_id is nullable in all three vendor schemas. Removing a visit and saving would emit UPDATE visits SET pet_id=NULL (dissociate) rather than DELETE, leaving an orphan row.
risks.mitigation: Add orphanRemoval=true to the Pet.visits association so the removed visit row is deleted (ADR 2026-08-05). This is the load-bearing mapping change without which the acceptance criteria pass in-memory but leak rows in the DB.

risks.risk: Removal-by-identity from a Set: Visit extends BaseEntity, which does not override equals/hashCode, so removal must locate the visit by getId() within pet.getVisits() and remove that exact element (identity), not construct a probe Visit.
risks.mitigation: Iterate pet.getVisits() to find the element whose id matches and remove it; do not rely on Set.remove(new Visit(id)).

notes: Verdict new (not minor) because cancellation is the app's first destructive/removal operation and introduces orphan-removal semantics plus a recorded cancellation-vs-status decision. ADR 2026-08-05-visit-cancellation-as-hard-delete records hard-delete over a cancelled-status field, keeping the sample free of lifecycle state per NG-5's rationale and the 'no undo' non-goal. The prd-entry explicitly deferred the hard-delete-vs-retained-state HOW to design; this ADR settles it. Optional TDD-refactor opportunity (not required): fold booking's inline date check in processNewVisitForm into !visit.isUpcoming() once the predicate exists, so both write paths share it. No design-doc-autofix records to audit this dispatch.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership guard chain is enforced server-side and is independent of the view affordance: loadOwnerAndPet/findPet throws when the pet does not belong to the path owner, and Pet.removeUpcomingVisit only iterates that pet's own visit collection, so a POST naming a visit that belongs to another owner's pet removes nothing (acceptance criterion 4).
Upcoming boundary is defense-in-depth: removeUpcomingVisit re-checks Visit.isUpcoming() on the server, so a crafted POST cannot cancel a past/today visit even though the th:if hides the button.
No new IDOR beyond the documented no-auth demonstration baseline; the guard chain prevents cross-owner/cross-pet visit removal via the path ids.
CSRF absence on the new POST matches the recorded baseline (no Spring Security, all mutations are open POSTs); the endpoint mirrors processNewVisitForm and does not weaken the baseline.

Mass assignment on the @ModelAttribute Owner bind is guarded: the controller's @InitBinder sets setDisallowedFields("id","*.id"), covering cancelVisit, so the aggregate cannot be re-pointed via request params before owners.save(owner).

No injection or XSS surface added: removal is via JPA orphan removal (no query string-building), and the template renders a static #{cancelVisit} message key plus integer path ids with Thymeleaf escaping intact.
Cross-request state is re-resolved: loadOwnerAndPet re-loads and re-validates the owner and pet from the repository on every request rather than trusting a prior request.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The ADR (2026-08-05-visit-cancellation-as-hard-delete.md) names orphanRemoval=true on Pet.visits as 'the load-bearing mapping change without which the acceptance criteria pass in-memory but leak rows in the DB.' All four cancel tests run under @WebMvcTest with a mocked OwnerRepository. They assert in-memory collection state (pet.getVisits().isEmpty()) and that save() was called on the mock — but the mock's save() does not execute JPA persistence. Removing orphanRemoval=true from Pet.java line 57 would not break any test in the suite, even though the ADR states that without it a cancelled visit is dissociated (pet_id set NULL) rather than deleted. The persistence semantic that justifies the ADR decision is completely unpinned. An integration test using the existing H2 datasource (e.g. a @SpringBootTest or @DataJpaTest slice) that deletes a visit and verifies no orphan row remains in the visits table is needed to make the hard-delete decision verifiable.

shouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit and shouldNotOfferCancelForAPastVisit both construct Visit objects directly via new Visit() / setId / setDate / setDescription. Testing-principles.md §Test Data Construction: 'Tests never call production constructors directly. Applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward.' VisitControllerTests already supplies a visit(int id, LocalDate date) factory. OwnerControllerTests needs an equivalent private helper and the two new tests should delegate to it.
findings.fix: Extract a private Visit factory method in OwnerControllerTests — e.g. private Visit visit(int id, LocalDate date) mirroring the one in VisitControllerTests — and replace the four direct-construction blocks in the two new tests with calls to it.

findings.description: upcoming.setId(20) and today.setId(21) are bare integer literals. In shouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit the value 20 is load-bearing — it appears verbatim in the URL fragment the assertion checks (pets/1/visits/20/cancel) — yet it carries no name explaining that relationship. Testing-principles.md §Three-Tier Data Naming: 'No mystery literals (bare 42, hello@x.com) — Tier 3 eliminated.' Both IDs should be promoted to named constants that make the role explicit.
findings.fix: Declare int upcomingVisitId = 20 (or a class-level constant) before use in shouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit and reference it in both setId and the containsString assertion. For shouldNotOfferCancelForAPastVisit the ID is irrelevant to the outcome; prefix it ANY_VISIT_ID to signal that.

findings.description: The prd-entry specifies test names (shouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit, shouldRemoveVisitFromRecordWhenCancelled, etc.) that use the should* prefix without the the{Subject} head required by testing-principles.md §Test Naming ('The naming school is BDD: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. Applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward'). The implementer followed the PRD names exactly. The conflict means either the PRD test_names field should not prescribe names at that level of detail, or the testing-principles naming school needs a documented carve-out for PRD-specified names. This is a brief defect, not an implementer error.

VisitControllerTests provides a visit(int id, LocalDate date) factory method used by all four cancel tests — factory-method discipline applied correctly in that file

title: Owner can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner record
summary: The owner detail page offers a cancel action beside each upcoming visit (dated later than today). Cancelling removes that visit from the pet's record. Past visits show no cancel action and stay immutable.
acceptance_criteria: Given an owner's record with a pet that has an upcoming visit, when the record is shown, then a cancel action is offered beside that visit.

notes: Supersedes the prd-entry at line 2 to correct one field only: test_names. Resolves the test-reviewer clarify finding at line 14. The line-2 names used the bare should* prefix (shouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit, etc.), which passes the layout.toml test_name_pattern mechanical floor but violates the BDD naming school in docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}, binding on tests written from 2026-07-31 onward). Decision: the naming school stands; no carve-out is warranted or possible — three durable sources already agree (testing-principles § Test Naming; the prd-authoring skill, which binds test_names to that school; and this schema's own example theResultShouldContainNewItems). author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The new test constructs Visit directly with `new Visit()` instead of via a factory method. Testing-principles § Test Data Construction / Factory Methods states that a slice adding a test writes it behind a factory from the start (binding from 2026-07-31 onward). ClinicServiceTests has no visit factory; add one (`private Visit visit(LocalDate date)`) following the same shape as the factory already in VisitControllerTests.
findings.fix: Add a private `visit(LocalDate date)` factory method to ClinicServiceTests that sets a description and returns the constructed Visit, then replace `new Visit()` / manual setters with a call to that factory.

findings.description: The local variable `int unknownVisitId = 999` introduces a bare integer literal for an irrelevant value. Testing-principles § Three-Tier Data Naming requires irrelevant values to carry a SOME_/ANY_ prefix or use an anonymous factory. VisitControllerTests does not yet have a class-level ANY_VISIT_ID constant. Add one (distinct from TEST_VISIT_ID = 100) and replace the bare 999.
findings.fix: Declare `private static final int ANY_VISIT_ID = 999;` at the class level (or any value != TEST_VISIT_ID), and replace the inline `int unknownVisitId = 999` with `int unknownVisitId = ANY_VISIT_ID`.
